goal_alignment.note: Real Citi Bike data for 2023 (yearly zip) and 2024 (12 monthly zips) was downloaded from s3.amazonaws.com/tripdata (output/download.log, tables/data_manifest.json). Outputs cover Q1 (seasonality), Q2 (weekday/weekend x hour), Q3 (member vs casual) and the optional Q4 (Open-Meteo weather, 731 days). No data was invented.

completeness.note: Scripts 01-04 and all expected tables and figures exist in the container (/app/code, /app/output). The 8 figures include fig_hourly_seasonal_robustness.png, which I did not open. correctness.note: Cleaning is plausible and reconciles: 79,410,195 raw rows, 38,596 removed (0.049%), 79,371,599 kept (cleaning_summary.csv, checks.json). Most removals are R5 >24h (37,576). All 643 non-positive durations fall on the two fall-back DST dates, which anomalies.md documents. Monthly, daily and hourly totals match, with 731 distinct dates. Seasonality tables match the figure I opened: 2023 peak Aug (3.96M), 2024 peak Oct (5.15M), troughs Jan/Feb. Peak/trough timing is not stable across years (bootstrap same-peak-month probability 0.55-0.88) and the tables say so. Weekday AM/PM peaks at 08:00 and 17:00 and the weekend peak at 15:00 agree across years. Casual share runs from about 11-13% in winter to about 23% in summer. Weather: Spearman rho 0.73 for temperature, -0.29 for precipitation, and HAC-based percent effects, all framed as association. Spot arithmetic checks out (35.08M/365 is about 96k per day; 44.29M/366 is about 121k). Minor inconsistencies: cleaning_summary.csv attributes clean rows by source-file year (35,079,756 / 44,291,843), while monthly_counts.csv uses the start-timestamp year (35,080,130 / 44,291,469). The 374-row difference is the spill-over documented in anomalies.md. Figure defects found on viewing: (1) fig_hourly_weekday_vs_weekend.png, panel B (2024): the y-axis is clipped at about 10.7k, so the 17:00 weekday peak (about 12.4k) runs off the top, the '08:00' label collides with the legend, and the panels share a y-axis set by 2023. (2) fig_monthly_volume.png panel A: the 'trough Jan 1.89M' and 'trough Feb 1.69M' annotations overlap. (3) fig_precip_vs_trips.png and fig_temp_vs_trips.png render fine. fig_heatmap_dow_hour.png, fig_member_vs_casual_hourly.png and fig_member_vs_casual_seasonal.png look legible and consistent with the tables.

traceability.note: Every number traces to a CSV/JSON in /app/output/tables, produced by scripts in /app/code with logs in /app/output/*.log. The manifest records URLs, sizes and sha256. The weather source URL, retrieval date and units are in weather_source.json. phases/research/research_loop.jsonl and the supervisor verdicts show the agent never visually inspected its figures (sandbox denials); I have now inspected 7 of 8, which closes most of that gap. summary: The research phase passes. It acquired the real 2023 and 2024 Citi Bike data (79.4M trips) and cleaned it with transparent per-rule counts (0.049% removed). It produced reconciled aggregate tables, bootstrap-CI analyses for seasonality, hour-by-weekday profiles and member-vs-casual differences, and an optional weather-association analysis that is described as association only. Numbers are internally consistent and match the figures I viewed. Two cosmetic figure defects remain (clipped y-axis in the 2024 hourly panel; overlapping trough labels), along with an unviewed robustness figure and a minor year-attribution inconsistency in cleaning_summary.csv. None of these changes the results, so analysis can proceed and should fix them.
recommendations: Fix fig_hourly_weekday_vs_weekend.png panel B: the y-axis is clipped at about 10.7k and the 2024 weekday 17:00 peak (about 12.4k) is cut off. Set ylim to cover the full CI band or use per-panel autoscale with a note, and move the 08:00 label away from the legend.
Fix overlapping 'trough Jan' and 'trough Feb' annotations in fig_monthly_volume.png panel A, for example by offsetting labels.
Open and check fig_hourly_seasonal_robustness.png, which was not viewed by the research agent or by this audit.

Make the year attribution consistent: cleaning_summary.csv per-year clean rows use the source-file year, while monthly_counts.csv uses the start-timestamp year (35,079,756 vs 35,080,130 for 2023). Add a one-line note, or report both in the report.

State the peak/trough instability in the report. The seasonal peak is Aug in 2023 but Oct (total) or Sep (per-day) in 2024, with same-peak-month bootstrap probabilities of 0.55-0.88. The robust claim is a summer-to-autumn plateau and a Jan/Feb trough with a peak/trough ratio of about 2.2-2.7. The 2024 level is higher (about 121k vs 96k trips per day), so avoid reading year-over-year growth as seasonal.

Keep causal language out of the weather finding. The temperature association is confounded by season: the month-FE model keeps about +3.7% per degree C, but within-month Spearman is only 0.34 and the Durbin-Watson statistic is 1.15, so intervals may be narrow.

Include the limitations already identified: DST artefacts on 4 dates; the member/casual definition and bike-type mix changing over time; single city and n=2 seasons; weather from a single reanalysis grid point; the R4 <60s sensitivity (only 182 extra rows, negligible).

Because container outputs are not on the host, copy the final report and figures to the host workspace (one plain 'docker exec ... cat file > host_path' per file; compound commands are denied). Scratch files audit_records/_fig_monthly.png and _f2.png to _f7.png were created by this audit and can be deleted.
